home.overline: Free · in your browser · nothing uploaded
home.lead: Read a short text out loud four times. You'll see what makes your voice hard to hear, and get settings that fit your mic and your room.
home.compat: Works best in Chrome or Edge · Ready-made settings for Wave Link + ReaPlugs · Open source on GitHub

how.lead: You read the same short text four times, and your browser compares the takes. It's like trying on the same shirt under different lights: the shirt stays the same, so every difference comes from the light. Here, the difference comes from your distance, your room and your effects.

takes.title: The four takes
takes.intro: You read the same short text four times. Each take starts with 3 seconds of quiet.
takes.raw: Three takes with just the mic, at 2, 8 and 15 cm (about a finger, a fist and an open hand away). Very close, the mic adds extra bass, like a radio host leaning in. Further away, it hears more of the room. Comparing them shows which distance sounds clearest for you.
takes.silence: 3 seconds of quiet first. While you stay silent, the page listens to the room on its own: how loud it is, and whether a fan, a fridge or traffic is humming along.
takes.fx: One take through your effects. You record it at your best distance and it's compared with the mic-only take, so you hear what your effects change: a before and after.

speech.def: Your voice level while you read. Too quiet, and people turn you up, room noise and all. Too loud, and it crackles.

noise.def: Measured in the 3 seconds of quiet: the hiss, hum and background sound when nobody is talking.

snr.def: How much louder your voice is than the room. Think of talking in a library versus a train station. A gap of 30 dB or more sounds clean.

tone.def: Your voice from deep to bright, compared with a typical voice, like checking the bass and treble on a stereo. It shows what's too strong or too weak.

tones.def: Steady whines or hums in the quiet part, like a fan, an air conditioner or a computer.

bandSnr.def: Voice over room for each part of your voice, from deep to bright. Turning up a part where the room is louder than you only makes the noise louder.

sibilance.def: How hissy your S and SH sounds are compared with the rest of your voice.

consistency.def: How much your volume jumps around while you read.

chain.title: The suggested settings
chain.intro: The settings are for the free ReaPlugs effects in Wave Link. Think of a car wash: each station does one job, in order. In a noisy room they run in the order below. In a quiet room ReaFIR is skipped and the order is ReaGate → ReaEQ → ReaComp.

ReaFIR.def: Listens to a few seconds of your quiet room, then takes that sound out of your voice, like noise-cancelling headphones for your mic. Only used in noisy rooms.

ReaEQ.def: Evens out the sound of your voice, like the bass and treble knobs on a stereo. It can also cut out a steady whine from a fan or machine.

ReaComp.def: Keeps your volume steady by gently turning down the loud parts, so quiet words aren't lost.

ReaGate.def: Turns the mic down between sentences so your pauses stay quiet, like a door that closes when you stop talking. In a noisy room it works gently, so it never cuts off words.

apply.title: Using the settings
apply.intro: Copy the suggested values from the Results page. Then pick one way:
apply.hand: By hand: open each effect window in Wave Link and type the values in.
apply.tool: With our tool: download the JSON file from Results, quit Wave Link from the tray (the small icons near the clock), then run {{cmd}}. It saves a backup of Settings.json first.
apply.reafir: ReaFIR is always set up by hand: it has to learn the noise of your room from a few seconds of quiet.

tips.title: Tips for noisy rooms
tips.closer: Get closer to the mic. Every time you halve the distance, your voice gets about 6 dB louder than the room, like talking across a table instead of across the room.
tips.aim: Turn the mic's deaf side toward the noise: the back of a cardioid mic, the sides of a supercardioid.
tips.off: Switch off fans, air conditioning and other machines while you record, if you can.
tips.boost: Don't turn up parts of your voice where the room is louder than you. It only makes the noise louder.
tips.target: Aim for your voice to be at least 30 dB louder than the room.

solutions.title: Shared settings
solutions.intro: Settings people shared for their mic, ranked by 👍 on GitHub. Votes mean people found them helpful, not that they are the best for you.

share.title: How to share
share.note: You need a GitHub account. The issue is public and contains no audio.
share.all: See all shared results on GitHub

privacy.lead: Everything is checked inside your browser. Nothing is uploaded unless you choose to share a summary.

local.title: On your computer
local.takes: Your recordings and their results are saved in this browser (in its IndexedDB storage).
local.prefs: Your choices, like your mic details, chosen inputs and last screen, are saved in this browser's localStorage.
local.noUpload: Nothing is uploaded to any server.
local.delete: Delete all on the Results page removes every take from this browser.

share.title: When you share
share.text: Sharing is always your choice. It opens a public GitHub issue under your own account with your mic details, the measured numbers and the suggested settings. It contains no audio, no device names and no dates, and you check it before posting.

remove.title: Removing a shared result
remove.text: Close or edit the issue on GitHub, or email <link>{{email}}</link> and ask for it to be removed from the community numbers.

tracking.title: No tracking
tracking.text: No analytics, no cookies, no ads.

tool.title: The Wave Link tool
tool.text: {{file}} runs on your own computer. It only reads and writes Wave Link's Settings.json, and saves a backup before changing it.
